requirements.requirement: Run an automated backup every night from node2's /srv/inventory/data to node1.
requirements.summary: Node2 has an active, enabled cron service and a daily 02:15 root cron entry invoking the backup script. Manual execution, including after node2 restarted, successfully transferred an archive to node1. The scheduled trigger itself was not observed firing at 02:15.

requirements.requirement: Store date-named archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1.
requirements.summary: Node1 contains inventory-2026-10-01.tar.gz in the required directory. It is nonempty, gzip-valid, mode 600, and contains the source data/ directory. Its checksum and validity persisted through node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain only the last seven days of inventory archives.
requirements.summary: The installed backup script deletes matching archives older than seven days using -mtime +6. A deliberately created eight-day-old archive was directly shown before execution and absent afterward, while the current archive remained.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered services and backup state. Node2 additionally completed a successful post-restart backup to node1.
limitations: The source directory was initially absent and remained empty, so the evidence validates archiving and transfer of the directory structure but not preservation of substantive file contents.
The actual overnight cron invocation was not observed; scheduling is established through the active cron service, installed entry, and successful direct execution of the same script.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account, directory, SSH-key, script, cron, and source-directory creation all support the backup outcome. The temporary eight-day-old archive was a bounded retention test and was removed by the intended rule (cmd-0c43e69e0e034963, cmd-f505221d0bbc4a9c). Both restarts were required by the provider protocol. Failed commands were read-only checks or a final listing failure after otherwise necessary setup; no unwanted residue is evidenced. Final snapshots show no failed services or package damage on either node.
